evidence: c5t12_s1952301689: collision at t=9.717 while robot moving 0.08 m/s; first unmapped point detected at t=4.73 at 1.0 m, bearing -21°, DWA active only until t≈5.03 (0.3 s window) → no avoidance.

c5t12_s2000876769: collision at t=51.7 while robot stopped; unmapped point entered 2 m range at t=48.35 (bearing -48°) but DWA deactivated after short debounce, so robot remained stationary and was hit.
c5t12_s471324936: stall abort at t=99.48 after 99 s with only 0.295 m movement; gap to tracked movers stayed > _SAFE_DIST and unmapped points never triggered DWA, leaving robot idle.

assumptions.assumption: Moving objects will be clustered into tracks (M) and used for avoidance
assumptions.why: In collisions (runs 1,2) the mover was not reliably tracked, so DWA never considered it.

assumptions.assumption: A 0.3 s DWA activation window is sufficient to plan safe motion until the threat passes
assumptions.why: Collisions occurred many seconds after the window closed, showing the window is too short.

assumptions.assumption: Margin base 0.15 m plus robot/mover radii provides enough safety buffer
assumptions.why: Collision at 0.56 m lateral offset indicates the margin was insufficient for fast‑approaching objects.

assumptions.assumption: Unmapped raw points filtered by _unmapped_raw correctly represent moving objects
assumptions.why: first_not_on_map timestamps show unmapped points were seen early, but they were not used persistently.

assumptions.assumption: Robot can resume normal waypoint following after a brief pause without re‑evaluating threats
assumptions.why: Threats persisted after pause, leading to collisions and stalls.

approach_families.family: simple pause based on unmapped points

candidates.idea: Make DWA persistent: reset st["dwa_until"] each step while any unmapped point is within _PF_RANGE, so DWA runs continuously until the threat clears.
candidates.for: Collisions where the short DWA window missed later approach of the same object.
candidates.risk: Higher CPU load; may cause oscillations if DWA keeps switching commands.

candidates.idea: Replace DWA with a Vector‑Field‑Histogram (VFH) reactive planner that builds a polar histogram from unmapped lidar points each cycle, selects the widest gap > robot width, and steers toward the goal through that gap.
candidates.for: Robust gap detection without relying on tracking; handles sudden appearance of moving boxes.
candidates.risk: May become overly conservative in cluttered aisles, causing stalls if no gap meets the width threshold.

candidates.idea: Hybrid approach: use the existing potential‑field to compute a desired heading, then feed that heading into a simplified DWA that only varies speed, keeping the heading fixed for the horizon.
candidates.for: Leverages successful PF heading while preserving DWA speed optimization.
candidates.risk: Complex interaction between PF and DWA could produce conflicting commands and instability.

diagnosis.chosen: VFH reactive planner was selected because it directly addresses the missed gap detection that caused collisions and does not depend on fragile tracking or short‑window activation.
diagnosis.target: controller logic and addition of VFH helper functions (histogram building, gap selection, steering command).
diagnosis.direction: 1. Add a function _vfh_histogram(pose, raw) that converts unmapped lidar points to polar bins (e.g., 5° resolution) and counts obstacles per bin. 2. Add _vfh_select_gap(hist) that finds the widest consecutive sequence of empty bins wider than the robot footprint plus safety margin and returns the central bearing. 3. In controller(), after _perceive() call _unmapped_raw() to get raw points and compute (hist, gap_bearing) via the new helpers. 4. If a gap exists, compute desired heading = yaw + gap_bearing and set w = _clamp(7.5*(desired_heading‑yaw), -_DWA_W_MAX, _DWA_W_MAX). 5. Compute v_nom from _follow() toward the waypoint, then limit v by _lidar_clear and by the distance to the nearest obstacle in that direction (e.g., v = min(v_nom, d_gap‑_R_ROBOT‑0.1)). 6. Run the final command through _guard() and return; otherwise, fall back to the original waypoint follower when no gap is found.
